Costumed Frank Review: The Mobster's Cold Case
Costumed Frank: The Mobster's Cold Case

Released in 2021, Costumed Frank (or "The Mobster") completely reimagines the hero's role. While the original was a blunt instrument of defense reduction, the Costume attempts to emulate the legendary 5-star hero

who aims to punish minion-heavy teams by stacking permanent frost damage and mana generation debuffs for every enemy (or minion) he kills. He’s a "Budget Skadi" for the 4-star arena, but does he have the muscle to pull off the job?

Frank trades his rags for riches, donning a pinstripe suit, fedora, and glasses. It’s a fantastic "mob enforcer" look that fits his nickname "The Mobster." The art implies a bit more sophistication than the base version—he's not just smashing things; he's "taking care of business." It’s arguably one of the better 4-star costume designs thematically, turning a monster into a hitman.
Even with the costume stat boost, Frank is fighting an uphill battle against modern stats.

targets to trigger his stacks, having an outdated attack stat makes his job incredibly difficult without massive support (attack buffs, defense down on enemies).

When released, players were excited for a "4-star Skadi." However, reality quickly set in: he just didn't hit hard enough to kill the minions of the era (Bera/Freya).

Modern minions (from heroes like the 5-star constructs or even modern 4-stars) have HP pools that far exceed Frank's damage cap. He is almost incapable of killing modern minions without an Attack Buff (e.g., from Boldtusk/Kiril) and Defense Down on the enemy (e.g., Grimm/Morel).

Costumed Frank is a mobster who talks a big game but often forgets to bring his gun. He tries to emulate the power of Skadi but lacks the raw stats to execute the hit. While the idea of stacking mana debuffs is tantalizing, the condition of "killing blows" is a hurdle too high for his modest attack stat. He’s a fun toy for specific Rush setups, but when the heat is on, you’re better off relying on the brute force of his original form.
Level the costume for the bonus, but keep the fedora in the closet unless you have a specific plan to make him work.
